title: schema.Fetcher cache never expires, so old schemas outlive a release
description: strspc-manager src/schema/schema.go: Fetch returns the file under os.UserCacheDir()/strspc/schemas whenever it exists; readCache checks only type and size, with no TTL or revalidation. After a schema release any machine with a cached entity/v1.json keeps failing RL002 on the new fields until the file is deleted. Reproduced 2026-10-30: on the real cache lint fails on inherits/overrides, with HOME pointing at an empty dir the same realm passes. Fix: add a TTL or conditional GET, keeping the stale copy as the offline fallback. Workaround: delete ~/Library/Caches/strspc/schemas (macOS).
notes:
Correction on the repro: the failing lint read the old cached entity/v1.json. That file was then rewritten at 09:58:05 by something other than the lint run, so lint passes on the real cache now. The defect stands from the code: readCache has no expiry, only replacing the file clears it.
The rewrite is explained: a parallel session deleted the stale entity/v1.json by hand during the 1.11.0 release, and its next validate refetched the file. Duplicate strspc-rules-cvk closed in favour of this bead.

title: strspc-manager: schema cache never expires, so published schema changes do not reach machines with a cached copy

After v1.11.0 reached steerspec.dev, strspc lint and realm validate still failed RL002 on an entity using inherits and overrides, because the cache held the copy from 2026-10-28; an isolated cache passed. title: pin-consumers.yml does not sync rules/_schema/ to consumers
description: pin-consumers.yml updates only the matrix files (rules/realm.json, .strspc/config.yaml and docs), never rules/_schema/. For 1.11.0 each consumer needed a hand-made sync PR (manager #156, CLI #152, sync #119, spec #18). strspc-manager v1.27.0 adds RM015, which compares a realm's _schema with its pinned core when a DependencyFetcher is supplied. Once the CLI wires that in, each core pin PR will likely fail the now-required 'rules / lint' check until _schema is synced. Fix: have pin-consumers copy rules/core/_schema/ from the release tag into each consumer's rules/_schema/ on the same PR.
design: tools/pin_core.py apply takes --schema-dir (core rules/core/_schema at the release tag). It overwrites each rules/_schema/*.json in the consumer that also exists in core, matching RM015 (config.v1 is not vendored, so it is not added). Fails if the consumer has no matching file. Same all-or-nothing write as the pins. If the pin is already X.Y.Z but a schema differs, it syncs and reports changed=true. pin-consumers.yml checks out strspc-rules at inputs.tag into a separate path, because a dispatch of an older tag runs from main. No token or permission change: create-pull-request already commits everything under consumer/. Update the PR body, AGENTS.md, README.md and the release skill. Tests in tools/tests/test_pin_core.py.
acceptance_criteria: A core release's pin PR in each consumer also updates rules/_schema/ to the tag, and rules / lint passes on it with RM015 active.

PR #95 open against develop. Depends on strspc-manager-h80 for the manager leg of the next release.
CLI develop has WithDependencyFetcher (#153), #154 promotes it. RM015 is a Warning but the org lint runs --strict, so drift fails rules / lint. All four consumers match v1.11.0 for bootstrap, entity.v1 and realm.v1 today, so the CLI release alone breaks nothing; the next core release with a schema change would.

title: GH#114: external standards references and coverage
description: Realms, entities and rules reference versioned external standards (OWASP ASVS, ECSS, IAB TCF) for provenance and for proving coverage to an auditor. Today only free-text reference notes exist. Full proposal in SteerSpec/strspc-rules#114.

Rule: standards clause references like owasp.asvs:2.1.1, prefix validated against the entity or realm declaration. Only state I rules count as evidence; P shows as mapped, not enforced. An overriding rule does not take on the replaced rule's mapping. Coverage report over the effective rule set. Release order: rules, manager, CLI.
acceptance_criteria: Rules define standards at realm, entity and rule level and the coverage semantics. realm.v1 and entity.v1 accept the fields. The five open questions are decided and recorded on GH#114. Manager lint rejects undeclared clause prefixes. CLI preserves the fields and provides the coverage report. KWRD declares RFC 2119.

PLB confirmed both uses (provenance and audit coverage) and asked to file on 2026-10-31. Open: whether SteerSpec holds full clause lists (licensing), mapping on Published rules, hash coverage, relation values, rule field name. Statement of applicability is out of scope, likely follow-up.
Decisions recorded on GH#114 on 2026-11-01: mapping is a standard note, not a rule field; add, revise, withdraw in any state with no rule revision; no clause lists; relation is implements or derived_from, required. Realm declaration sits in the realm object. KWRD declaration moves to step 4.
Draft rules are in PR 125. Manager step, from the adversarial review: realm-lint owns NTE-015 (checkSubRealms holds parent and sub-realm); rulelint must skip rather than fail realm tiers; warn for manifest-less sources and for a sub-realm source without its parent; keep standard out of both relationNoteTypes maps; exclude standard notes from CacheKey; call inherit.Effective with nil states and filter afterwards; walk all tree entities, since Inheritance skips those without inherits; apply discards replaced notes, so keep a replaced list and walk each hop's Overrides recursively; evaluate relation per note; rulerefs flags mitre.cwe:CWE-787 style content as RF001 in rendered notes, so treat declared ids as non-realm qualifiers. Open wording point for STDREF-009 and 010: tie the Note to the implements Reference (same id and version with different relations in parent and child).
PR 125 rule numbers moved: coverage rule set STDREF-010, identity 011, covered 012, mapped 013, lapsed 014 and 015, override 016; note rules NTE-013 to NTE-019. The wording point above is closed: mapped and lapsed now tie the Note to its own implements Reference. Manager also needs an RD check for NTE-018: rule revision moved with the body unchanged. The bead's earlier note uses the old numbers.
Schema step: entity.v1 and realm.v1 need minItems 1 on standards and minLength 1 on version and url, because omitempty hides empty values from the structs and lint can't see them. Add a standard note to the manager's testdata/clean with the core pin. CLI step: its next-step hints omit --recursive, so RL029 is missed without it; strspc lint on single files never reaches RL029.
Correction to the CLI step note: RL031 (was RL029) now runs in realm validate with or without --recursive, so the CLI hints need no change for it. Standards codes moved to RL028 to RL031 after strspc-manager PR 223 took RL026 and RL027.

title: Make the override and inheritance rules ready to Publish (assessment 2026-11-25)
description: Assessment of dev.steerspec.core at e62fee9 (v1.25.0 plus #197) found the override model (RUL-018 to RUL-023, NTE-042 to NTE-044, ENT-011 to ENT-019) not ready to be Published. design:
# dev.steerspec.core assessment before the next release (2026-11-25)

Scope: develop at e62fee9, which is v1.25.0 (already tagged and on main) plus #197. The release in question is the one after 1.25.0.

Method: read all 251 rules and their Notes; scripted the citation and supersession graph; built a sandbox with an upstream realm, an organisation realm that inherits and overrides it, a grandchild Entity, a Standard Realm and a consumer project, and ran strspc 1.41.1 on it.

## Verdict

- The release can be cut. Everything #197 adds is Draft. Lint, realm validate and diff against v1.25.0 are clean, and CI and Build Schema passed on e62fee9.
- The override model (RUL-018 to RUL-023, NTE-042 to NTE-044, ENT-011 to ENT-019) is not ready to be Published.
- The release unblocks strspc-manager-wcj. Findings 1, 2 and 7 change what the manager builds, so settle them in Draft text first.

## Inheritance and overriding

### Settle before the release

1. **RUL-021 against consumer configuration.** A Published override of an Implemented rule is enforced as Implemented.
   - SPCFG-009 and SPCFGFAIL-002 filter on "rule lifecycle state codes". Nothing says they read the enforced state, so `evaluate_on: [I]` may drop both the override and its target.
   - SPCFG-008 says the consumer, not the rule, sets severity; with `fail_on: [I]` a Published rule now fails the run.
   - Published has no unenforced window for such an override, against the guidance of RULST-009/02. A stricter override has to stay Draft until the code complies.
   - A dependency bump in which upstream promotes the target to Implemented starts enforcing the child's Published override with no change in the child.
   - The first commit of #197 used the other design (an override applies once its state reaches the target's) and it was reworked after review. Under that design the same bump would silently bring the inherited rule back, so the merged design is the more stable one.
   - Remedy: Draft edits. State that `evaluate_on` and `fail_on` read the enforced state, and add a Note on the missing Published window.
2. **strspc-manager-wcj is stale.** Its title and description describe the dropped design ("once it reaches the target's state"). Rewrite it from RUL-018 to RUL-023 before anyone implements it.
7. **Coverage drops when an override is Published.** STDREF-010 removes the inherited rule, and STDREF-012 counts only state Implemented.
   - Sandbox, 1.41.1: an inherited Implemented rule covered clause 4.1. A Published override with its own `standard` Note turned it to "mapped"; without the Note it was "lapsed".
   - Under RUL-021 that override is enforced as Implemented, so the figure falls while enforcement does not.
   - Remedy: Draft edit to STDREF-012, or accept the drop and say so in a Note.

### Settle before these rules are Published

3. **"Effective rule set" is never defined.** ENT-009, RUL-009, RUL-018 and RUL-019 use it. Two readings exist for chains: the parent's set net of its own overrides, or not. The manager uses the netted reading (a grandchild inherited the parent's Published override, and RR015 rejected overriding the original target). Remedy: one new Draft rule defining the term, since ENT-009 and RUL-009 are Published.
4. **Two words for one thing.** RUL-009, RUL-018, RUL-020, RUL-021, NTE-042 and STDREF-015 say "replaces"; RUL-019 and STDREF-010 say "takes precedence over". Draft RUL-018 also contradicts the unconditional "replaces" of Published RUL-009. Remedy: Draft edits, and consider superseding RUL-009.
5. **Upstream changes to an overridden rule.** No core rule covers it.
   - Sandbox: when upstream published a successor, the child inherited the overridden rule and the unmodified successor together.
   - When upstream retired the target, the child held the successor and its own former override side by side. `strspc check` warned (RR016); `realm validate`, `lint` and `render` did not.
   - A Published override can't be retargeted (RUL-007). Superseding it with a rule that names the successor worked in the CLI, but RUL-011 only speaks of restating the same target.
   - The sandbox dependency was an unpinned local path, so this models the state after a bump, not the bump.
   - Remedy: new Draft rules for a dead override and for retargeting through supersession.
6. **Superseding an override.** RUL-019 keeps a Published or Implemented predecessor in precedence while its successor is Draft. What is missing is when the "lapses" of RUL-011 takes effect for a successor that drops `overrides`. Remedy: new Draft rule.
8. **Adopting a standard is unspecified.** The standards design names an "adopt" model (inheriting a standard's text as a project's own rules) as a non-goal, to come after #35.
   - Nothing forbids it today: the sandbox Entity inherited and overrode a Standard Realm Entity with no diagnostic.
   - Adopted rules are never Implemented (STDRLM-010) and never evaluated (STDRLM-011), so they enforce nothing.
   - An override of one gets no clause link: STDREF-016 maps it only by its own `standard` Notes, and Standard Realm rules carry `clause`, not Notes.
   - The path that exists for enforcing a standard is a Standard Reference with a `realm`, the organisation's own rules with `standard` Notes, and `exclusion` Notes.
9. **The upstream owner's controls are coarse and Draft.**
   - Visibility is per Entity and defaults to `public`, core's own Entities included. ENT-011 to ENT-019 are Draft while `inherits` and `overrides` are Published.
   - There is no per-Rule lock. ENT-015 and ENT-019 make a chain as narrow as its narrowest Entity, and inheritance is single, so one child can't derive from a baseline that mixes locked and tailorable rules.
   - A child of a `protected` Entity that omits `visibility` defaults to `public` and fails ENT-015 (RR024 in the sandbox).
11. **`override_ack` records an act, not an approval.** "A contributor of its Realm" adds nothing to CTRB-005, the author can acknowledge their own rule, and same-realm overrides need it too. A Draft edited after it was acknowledged needs a second Note, since NTE-044 freezes the first.

### Later

10. **No waiver.** Tailoring is add, extend (`extends` Note) or replace. An inherited rule can't be declared not applicable; the workaround is an override with a MAY body, which coverage reports as lapsed.
12. **Derivation is per Entity.** Parent sub-entities aren't inherited (ENT-006/01) and EUIDs can't collide with a dependency (RLM-006), so a 20-Entity baseline needs 20 child Entities. Chains stop at three hops (ENT-008).
13. **Retired.** RULST-010 says a Retired rule is still in force. Notes ENT-006/01 and ENT-019/01 say it is not, and ENT-009 doesn't inherit it. Revise the Notes.
14. **Tooling.** `realm validate --recursive --strict` reported nothing where `render` printed RR015, RR023 and RR024, and where `check` printed RR016. This is a strspc-manager issue.
15. **Identity providers.** CTRB-002/01 lists only `github`, and CTRB-002 and CTRB-003 are Implemented. An organisation on another provider can't author compliant rules. Goes with #135.

## Decisions

1. Keep "precedence from Published, enforced as Implemented" and close its gaps (findings 1 and 7)? Recommended: yes.
2. Adopting a Standard Realm Entity: forbid `inherits` until the adopt model is designed, or specify it now? Recommended: forbid for now.
3. Per-Rule lock, or visibility per Entity only? Recommended: per Entity for now, with an inheriting Entity defaulting to the inherited Entity's visibility.
4. A waiver for an inherited rule, or keep the MAY override? Recommended: keep the override for now.
5. `override_ack`: keep as a marker, or require a contributor other than the rule's author? Recommended: keep as a marker until #135.

## Rest of the rule set

- 251 rules: 131 Draft, 32 Published, 78 Implemented, 9 Retired, 1 Abandoned.
- STDREF (28), STDRLM (21) and STDCWK (7) are all Draft while CI coverage gates depend on STDREF (#185).
- NTE-007 to NTE-019 are Draft. NTE-005/01, on an Implemented rule, cites NTE-008 to NTE-011. RLMMNFST-004/01, on a Published rule, cites Draft RLM-015 and RLIFRMT-008.
- No Published or Implemented rule body cites a Draft, Abandoned or missing rule.
- RULST-011 is Abandoned, so no core rule lists the allowed transitions; RULST-012 stands alone.
- RUL-009/01 and RULST-008 predate RULST-012 (strspc-rules-aop).
- RL027 info on Draft RLMMNFST-006, RLMMNFST-008 and RLMMNFST-010.
- All 9 Retired rules have an Implemented successor.

## Not tested

- RUL-018 to RUL-023: strspc 1.41.1 predates #197 and applies a Draft override at once.
- `tools/build-schema.py --check` locally (`jsonschema` is missing); the Build Schema workflow passed on e62fee9.
- AI evaluation on the sandbox.
- A Standard Reference linked to a Standard Realm.
- The only real override in the org is GOTEST-002 in strspc-manager, same-realm and Draft. Cross-realm overrides are unexercised outside the sandbox.

title: GH#207: add refs.coverage to config.v1 for rule-citation coverage
description:
SteerSpec/strspc-rules#207, step 1 of SteerSpec/strspc-CLI#261 (strspc-manager#391 is step 2). Prompts, agent instructions and docs list rule IDs by hand and nothing fails when a rule is added; the fix is a coverage check declared in .strspc/config.yaml. The config schema root has additionalProperties false, so a refs key fails validation today.

Add an optional refs object (additionalProperties false) with refs.coverage, an array of at least one item. Each item (additionalProperties false) has entities (required, non-empty array of entity IDs, the existing entity ID pattern), files (required, non-empty array of glob strings in the syntax strspc refs already uses) and states (optional, array of lifecycle state codes, reusing the definition fail_on and evaluate_on use; strspc-CLI would default to D, P and I).

To decide: whether an SPCFG rule should describe the section. config.v1.schema.json is generated by tools/build-schema.py, so the change goes there. Ships in a core release (minor: new schema capability).
acceptance_criteria: config.v1.schema.json accepts a refs.coverage section of the shape in GH#207 and rejects unknown keys at each level; tools/build-schema.py --check passes; tests cover the new section; the change is released in a core version.
